front: Tu es libre samedi soir ?
back: Are you free on Saturday night?
context: The classic first step before an invitation.

front: Ça te dirait de venir dîner à la maison ?
pronunciation: [sah tuh dee-reh duh vuh-neer dee-nay ah lah meh-ZOHN]
back: Would you like to come for dinner at our place?
context: 'Ça te dirait de…?' = would you like to…? Friendly and polite.

front: On pourrait aller au cinéma.
back: We could go to the cinema.
context: Conditional to suggest: on pourrait, on devrait.

front: Et si on allait à la plage ?
pronunciation: [ay see ohn nah-leh ah lah PLAZH]
back: How about going to the beach?
context: 'Et si on' + imparfait = how about…? Very common suggestion structure.

front: Avec plaisir !
back: With pleasure!
context: Warm acceptance. Also: 'Volontiers !'

front: Volontiers, c'est gentil.
back: Gladly, that's kind of you.
context: 'Volontiers' = gladly, willingly.

front: Bonne idée, je suis partant !
back: Good idea, count me in!
context: 'Être partant(e)' = to be up for it.

front: Désolé, je ne peux pas, j'ai déjà quelque chose de prévu.
pronunciation: [day-zoh-LAY, zhuh nuh puh PAH, zhay day-zhah kel-kuh shohz duh pray-VÜ]
back: Sorry, I can't, I already have plans.
context: 'Avoir quelque chose de prévu' = to have something planned. A polite way to decline.

front: Ce week-end, ça ne va pas être possible.
pronunciation: [suh wee-KEND, sah nuh vah pah zeh-truh poh-SEE-bluh]
back: This weekend won't be possible.
context: A softer refusal than 'je ne peux pas'.

front: Une autre fois, peut-être ?
back: Another time, maybe?
context: Softens a refusal and keeps the door open.

front: Je te dis ça demain, d'accord ?
back: I'll let you know tomorrow, OK?
context: Like 'je vais voir', it can be a polite way of not committing.

front: On se retrouve où ?
back: Where shall we meet?
context: 'Se retrouver' = to meet (as planned).

front: Rendez-vous devant la gare à dix-neuf heures.
back: Let's meet in front of the station at 7 p.m.
context: 'Rendez-vous' = meeting point/time (also a date or an appointment).

front: À quelle heure on se voit ?
back: What time shall we meet?
context: 'Se voir' = to see each other.

front: Ça te va, vingt heures ?
back: Does 8 p.m. work for you?
context: 'Ça te va ?' = does that suit you?

front: Parfait, ça me va très bien.
back: Perfect, that suits me fine.
context: 'Ça me va' = that works for me.

front: Je t'envoie l'adresse par message.
back: I'll text you the address.
context: 'Un message', 'un texto', 'un SMS'. On WhatsApp: 'je t'envoie un message sur WhatsApp'.

front: J'organise une fête pour mon anniversaire.
back: I'm throwing a party for my birthday.
context: 'Une fête' or 'une soirée' = a party.

front: Tu veux que j'apporte quelque chose ?
back: Do you want me to bring something?
context: Polite guests offer to bring something: a bottle of wine, a dessert, flowers.

front: Apporte juste ta bonne humeur !
back: Just bring your good mood!
context: A friendly reply meaning 'nothing needed'.

front: Désolé, je vais être un peu en retard.
pronunciation: [day-zoh-LAY, zhuh veh zeh-truh an puh ahn ruh-TAR]
back: Sorry, I'm going to be a bit late.
context: Arriving 10–15 minutes late to a dinner at someone's home is normal in France ('le quart d'heure de politesse').

front: On remet ça à la semaine prochaine ?
pronunciation: [ohn ruh-meh SAH ah lah suh-men proh-SHEN]
back: Shall we postpone it to next week?
context: 'Remettre' = to postpone. Also 'reporter'.

front: J'ai un empêchement, on peut décaler ?
back: Something's come up, can we reschedule?
context: 'Un empêchement' = something that prevents you. 'Décaler' = to move (a time).

front: Merci pour l'invitation !
back: Thanks for the invitation!
context: Say it when accepting and again when leaving.

front: Ça me ferait très plaisir de te voir.
pronunciation: [sah muh fuh-reh treh pleh-ZEER duh tuh VWAHR]
back: I'd love to see you.
context: 'Faire plaisir à quelqu'un' = to make someone happy.

front: On se fait un resto ce week-end ?
pronunciation: [ohn suh feh tan res-TOH suh wee-KEND]
back: Shall we go out for a meal this weekend?
context: Informal: 'se faire un resto / un ciné' = to treat yourselves to a meal / a film.

front: Je suis dispo jeudi, et toi ?
back: I'm free on Thursday, what about you?
context: 'Dispo' = disponible (available), informal.

front: On fait un apéro chez moi vendredi ?
pronunciation: [ohn feh tan nah-pay-ROH shay MWAH vahn-druh-DEE]
back: Shall we have drinks at my place on Friday?
context: 'L'apéro' (apéritif) = early-evening drinks and snacks: a French institution.

front: Viens avec qui tu veux.
back: Bring whoever you want.
context: 'Qui tu veux' = whoever you want.

front: C'est une soirée déguisée, n'oublie pas ton costume !
pronunciation: [seh tün swah-ray day-ghee-ZAY, noo-blee pah tohn kos-TÜM]
back: It's a costume party, don't forget your costume!
context: 'Se déguiser' = to dress up.

front: Je vous invite au restaurant pour fêter ma promotion.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo zan-veet oh res-toh-RAHN poor feh-tay mah proh-moh-SYOHN]
back: I'm taking you to a restaurant to celebrate my promotion.
context: 'Inviter' implies you're paying.

front: Ça tient toujours pour demain ?
back: Are we still on for tomorrow?
context: 'Ça tient toujours ?' = is it still on?

front: Oui, c'est toujours d'actualité.
back: Yes, it's still on.
context: 'Être d'actualité' = to still be relevant/on.

front: On a passé une super soirée, merci encore !
pronunciation: [ohn nah pah-say ün sü-pehr swah-RAY, mehr-see ahn-KOR]
back: We had a great evening, thanks again!
context: A message the next day is a nice touch.

front: La prochaine fois, c'est chez nous !
back: Next time, it's at our place!
context: Returning the invitation is expected in French social life.
